compliance: Protected variety (labelled cov; US PP25,915); propagation for sale needs a licence.
cvs: 'Aurea' – golden-yellow leaves · f. angustifolia – narrow, willow-like leaves
foliage: evergreen; aromatic, glossy dark green lance-shaped leaves
hardinessNote: Hardy through an average UK winter, approximately -10 to -5°C; pot-grown plants need shelter in hard frosts.
pollination: not applicable; grown for foliage, the species bears male and female flowers on separate plants
prune: Trim to shape in summer. Cut out frost-browned shoots in late spring once new growth shows.
resilience: Copes well with clipping and pot culture; leaves scorch in cold winds and hard frost. Pests: bay sucker, scale insects, leaf spot.
toxicity: Leaves are a culinary herb for people, but bay is listed as toxic to dogs, cats and horses if eaten, causing vomiting and diarrhoea. Not the same plant as cherry laurel.
uncertain: size: RHS 2.5–4 m; Promesse de Fleurs 1.5–2 m; US nurseries about 2.4 × 1.8 m — compact for a bay but not small
hardiness: RHS calls it borderline hardy; H4 kept, matching the deck's Laurus nobilis
compliance: UK/EU PBR number not found; US patent PP25,915
uses: Patio containers · herb gardens · small gardens · culinary leaves · formal clipped shapes
visual: Compact, dense, aromatic evergreen bay · glossy dark green culinary leaves all year · small yellowish spring flowers
water: Water pots regularly in summer and keep them barely moist in winter. Plants in the ground need little once established.
